trust_decision.summary: Container nesting deeper than the interpreter can recurse must be rejected as an IonException (recoverable, like other malformed input) rather than escape as RecursionError/crash. At the pinned commit this is already decided in simpleion.py's _translate_recursion_error wrapper around every load/dump path, and in ioncmodule.c via Py_EnterRecursiveCall.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'uncontrolled recursion in the Ion reader'; the recursive _load in simpleion.load_python is the obvious recursion on nesting.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Not applicable: the published fix commit changes no source logic (fix.diff:24-37 are version-string bumps only); the recursion protection is already present in the pinned tree.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Direct use of the public low-level reader API (blocking_reader(managed_reader(binary_reader()))) on nested annotation wrappers recurses _annotation_handler -> _tlv_parser with no IonException translation; only simpleion wraps it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Low-level reader API is a raw event coroutine; callers of it are outside the simpleion load/dump surface the protection is documented on.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module from simpleion.py, same package

O9_family: CWE-674 uncontrolled recursion (nesting-depth DoS / exception-type contract)
